Project: aeg, aeg-core
Iteration: aeg-forge-state-v1 · task 7

**Boundary** — The final cutover: delete the ~44 files that migrated to forge-native homes in tasks 3/4 (all `aeg-root/iterations/*.md` topology files — active and `completed/`, all `*.tokens.md` ledgers) — the moment the "birth rule" (`iterations/README.md`) actually completes: "gates read files until the migration flips the config in one deliberate act." This task IS that act. NOT: the kept-file trio (already moved in task 2, not deleted) — this task deletes only what tasks 3/4 proved has a working forge-native replacement.

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (every gate, every Studio page, every Archivist automation path proven working on the new sources with the old files STILL present in tasks 3/4/5 — this task is the final "now remove the crutch" step, provable by: delete, re-run the full gate suite + Studio smoke test, confirm nothing references the deleted paths).

**Project(s) + blast radius** — aeg, aeg-core. This is the point where every other active/future iteration's dispatch gates are running purely forge-native — full-repo re-verification is mandatory, not a formality.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: 3, 4, 5` — all three cutovers (gates, ledgers/lessons/state, Studio) must be proven live BEFORE their file sources are removed. Deleting first and finding a missed consumer after is exactly the failure this task ordering exists to prevent.

**Traps to avoid** — Do a final repo-wide grep for the deleted paths immediately before merging — a reference missed by tasks 2/3/4/5's own grep-sweeps is the single most likely failure mode this late in the migration. Archive `completed/` topology files too, not just active ones — per the birth rule, "history never migrates — ring 2 reads the past where it lies," so consider whether truly historical `completed/*.md` files should be deleted at all, or kept as a frozen archive exempt from this task (Brief Author's dig should resolve this explicitly — Planner default: keep `completed/` as historical record, delete only ACTIVE topology files whose forge-native replacement is live).

**Suggested agent-class** — high: the capstone task; a missed reference here is the worst possible time to find one.

**Stop-and-escalate** — Any surviving reference to a deleted path found post-delete is a hard stop, not a follow-up ticket.

**Docs to keep coherent** — `iterations/README.md`'s birth-rule section (state it as COMPLETE, not aspirational), `state-machine.md`, `enforcement.md`, `coordination.md` — every doc describing "files read until migration" now describes the post-migration reality. Decision log entry recording the cutover's completion date (Tier 3 — this is the single most consequential completion event in the whole program).

Rewire Studio's data-loading to use task 1's adapter (Milestone + labeled Issues + Issue rationale) for everything it currently gets from the file, keeping its EXISTING rendering/components untouched (this is a data-source swap, not a redesign). NOT: any visual/UX change; NOT `apps/vinaya/web` (a separate, already-planned copy in `vinaya-studio-v1` — this task is THIS repo's OWN existing Studio, still living at `apps/aeg/web`).

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (every Studio page that currently renders iteration/task state renders IDENTICALLY after the swap — a before/after screenshot or snapshot-test comparison per page), bounded surface (`src/lib/aeg-fs/**`, the iteration/task detail pages, `src/lib/forge/**` if it needs to compose with the new adapter), single failure mode (a page silently renders blank/wrong once the file source is gone).

NOT: relocating any per-project decision log (`apps/*/specs/*-decisions.md` — those stay put; this task is the root-level trio only, per D-110's scope) — Planner note for Brief Author: confirm at dig time whether extending this to per-project logs is in scope or a follow-up; D-110 didn't explicitly resolve this and it's a real ambiguity to flag, not assume. NOT: any behavior change — every gate must produce byte-identical output before/after, just reading a different path.

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (every gate that parses decisions/projects/doc-owners produces identical output against the new path; `git mv` preserves history), one agent holds it, bounded surface (3 files moved + path updates across a known, greppable set of consumers), single failure mode (a stale hardcoded path silently breaks a gate).

**Traps to avoid** — This is a `git mv`, not a copy-then-delete — preserve file history. Grep for EVERY string literal reference to the old paths before considering this done — a single missed hardcoded path (e.g. in a role doc's prose, a CI workflow's `cat` command, a husky hook) silently breaks that one consumer with no immediate signal. Do not extend scope to per-project decision logs without flagging the ambiguity (see Boundary) — that's a bigger, separate decision (do all `apps/*/specs/*-decisions.md` move too, or only the root trio?) that D-110 didn't resolve explicitly.

**Suggested agent-class** — mid: mechanical, well-bounded, no novel design — but the grep-sweep discipline matters more than cleverness here.

**Stop-and-escalate** — If any consumer can't be cleanly repointed (e.g. a script assumes the file lives at repo root for path-relative reasons beyond a simple constant), stop (`severity:execution`).

Confirmed no consumers outside `packages/aeg-core` + `apps/aeg`. Every one of these must be repointed in the SAME PR that moves the files — this task is not "done" until every real consumer above compiles and passes against the new path, not just the ones originally named in Boundary.

body:
Project: aeg-core
Iteration: aeg-forge-state-v1 · task 1

**Boundary** — Build the generic, repo-parameterized forge-reading adapter: a NEW package (`packages/forge-state`, name final at brief time) holding the only octokit/`gh`-calling code in this migration — reads a Milestone's title/description/state (Goal + Lifecycle), reads `iteration:<slug>`-labeled Issues for task membership (unchanged mechanism — already forge-native today), and parses `Depends-on`/`Conflicts-with` edges from Issue rationale bodies, HARDENED against the multi-value-as-separate-prose-spans gap the 2026-07-06 spike found (Issue #383's own body: `Depends-on: 1` (...), `2` (...) — two backtick spans, not one comma-joined value). Repo/owner are parameters, not hardcoded — every future consumer (this repo's own gates, later `vinaya-cli-v1`'s `apps/vinaya/sources`) passes them in. NOT: touching any existing `packages/aeg-core/bin/*` gate (task 3's job); NOT the file-backed side (nothing to build — the existing file readers already exist); NOT a `packages/aeg-core` change — this adapter's I/O disqualifies it from that package's post-#372 purity charter.

**Sizing** — Passes: one verification story (given a repo+owner+iteration-slug, the adapter derives the identical task list + dependency graph a human reading the topology file would see — golden comparison against every currently active iteration, not a fixture), one agent holds it, bounded surface (one new package), single failure mode (adapter produces wrong/incomplete state).

**Project(s) + blast radius** — aeg-core (registry entry only, if this package is later registered as a project — Planner note, not required for task 1 itself). No existing consumer touched; this is wholly new, additive code.

**Dependency rationale** — `Depends-on: —`. First task; independently buildable and testable before any live gate is touched.

**Traps to avoid** — Do NOT let this leak into `packages/aeg-core` — that package is zero-I/O by charter (task 28, #372); network/API calls belong only in this new package. Do NOT hardcode `daniboomerang/attalabs` anywhere in the adapter's core logic — every call site must pass repo/owner explicitly, even though every current CALLER happens to be this one repo (this is the exact reuse this whole resequencing is for — `vinaya-cli-v1` later imports or re-homes this package, not rewrites it). Parser must tolerate BOTH the topology file's `1, 2` comma-joined form AND Issue-rationale prose's multiple separate backtick-quoted numeric tokens for the same field — test both shapes explicitly, using #383's real body as a fixture. Milestone lookup must handle "no Milestone yet for this iteration" gracefully (early iterations may not have one) — this is a real transitional state during rollout, not an error.

**Suggested agent-class** — high: the architectural keystone of the entire migration; gets reused by a second, different product later.

**Stop-and-escalate** — If Milestone description length limits (GitHub caps description length) can't hold a realistic Goal text, stop (`severity:strategy`) — that's a real product constraint, not a detail to paper over. If the golden comparison diverges for any currently active iteration, stop — a divergence is a design finding, never something to silently reconcile.

**Docs to keep coherent** — New package needs a README stating its scope (this repo's migration tool AND the future Vinaya CLI's reusable dependency — name both consumers explicitly so its generic-by-design requirement isn't lost). `docs-index.md` regenerated.
